page: Amazon Web Services c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier performance across multiple workloads. The instance achieves top 10% placement in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU performance. It also registers top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and image and text processing. Passmark database operations and LLM inference for text generation using a 7B model also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput consistently place in the top 25%.

The c8a.8xlarge offers high compute density and memory speed, making it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, and the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. This instance is well-suited for high-performance computing, software compilation, database operations, web serving, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference.
